newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ATHLETICS-BROWN AND NEGURA CAPTURE EUROPEAN CROSS COUNTRY TITLES.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BROWN AND NEGURA CAPTURE EUROPEAN CROSS COUNTRY TITLES.

text.p: Britain's Jon Brown sped to victory in the European Cross Country Championships in the Belgian town of Charleroi on Sunday, covering the muddy 9.65 km course in 32 minutes 37 seconds.
Brown took control during the opening kilometre, shrugging off the challenge of Paulo Guerra from Portugal, the champion for the last two years.
The 25-year-old from Sheffield came home 35 seconds clear of his nearest rival to record the largest winning margin in the history of the event.
Guerra ran alone for much of the race to take the silver medal in 33 minutes 12 seconds with the bronze going to Mustapha Essaid from France seven seconds further back.
Portugal took the men's team title with 27 points, with three men finishing in the top ten. France were second with 47 points and hosts Belgium were third with 59 points.
Romania's Iulia Negura added to her list of accolades with a impressive victory in the women's 4.55km.
The 29-year-old, the 1990 and 1991 World 15km road race champion, broke away from Sweden's Sara Wedlund around 800 metres from home and crossed the line in 16 minutes 58 seconds.

The Swedish runner had to settle for silver medal for the second year in succession, finishing six seconds adrift of Negura. Julia Vaquero from Spain overhauled Annemari Sandell from Finland, the defending champion, close to the line to capture the bronze medal.
France were the surprise women's team winners with 30 points, just ahead of Romania with 33 points and Britain with 42 points.
